sections.heading: C2 — Motorcycles, mopeds, bicycles, autocycles, confusables and KG hints
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Motorcycles, mopeds, bicycles, autocycles, confusables and KG hints

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: FXP0069
A fast vehicle's wind blast can startle a rider or push them off balance, raising the chance of a crash [FXP0069] [A04].
Why it matters: group riders; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec12-F11 [FXP0069]
Source: [FXP0069 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A04
A rider moving to one side of the lane, checking over a shoulder, or leaning the vehicle is probably about to turn, in addition to any turn or hand signal you see. [A04]
Why it matters: group riders; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A04
A rider's single headlight or taillight can blend into the lights of other traffic, so look carefully. [A04]
Why it matters: group riders; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables sec12-R05 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A04
Before changing lanes and again after passing, check your blind spot for a rider and be sure you can see them clearly in the rearview mirror before moving back. [A04]
Why it matters: group riders; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A04
Opening a car door into the path of approaching traffic, including motorcycles and bicycles, is dangerous and illegal; check mirrors and open the door with your right hand. [A04]
Why it matters: group riders; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A04
It is illegal for a motorist to drive beside a motorcyclist or pass one within the same lane; use the adjacent lane when legal and safe. [A04]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-F29 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A04
Most vehicle-motorcycle crashes happen at intersections and on busy city streets. [A04]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-F30 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A04
Motorcycles with engines of 125cc or more may legally use freeways and limited-access highways. [A04]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-R11 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A04
A motorcycle's single headlight and small profile can make it seem farther away and slower than it is, a risk that grows at night and in bad weather. [A04]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-R03 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A04
Motorcyclists often slow by engine braking and downshifting, which does not light the brake lights, so keep extra space, and use your horn sparingly so you do not startle riders. [A04]
Why it matters: group motorcycles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables none [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A04
Under Michigan law a moped has two or three wheels, an engine of no more than 100 cc, a top speed of no more than 30 mph on level ground, and no gear shifting by the rider. [A04]
Why it matters: group mopeds; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-R08 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A04
Scooter is a general term covering mopeds and also more powerful two-wheelers that fall outside the moped definition. [A04]
Why it matters: group mopeds; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-R11 [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A05
Bicyclists may ride on any Michigan road except limited-access freeways, anywhere in the lane as long as they ride with traffic, with the same rights and duties as motorists. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-R08 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A05
Before turning right or pulling off the road, look for bicyclists coming up from behind on the shoulder or in a bike lane, and let them pass first when appropriate. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A05
Never use a bike lane as a right-turn lane, and do not pass a bicyclist and then turn right in front of them unless it is safe. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A05
Michigan law requires at least 3 feet of space when passing a bicyclist; if that is impractical, pass at a safe distance and speed, and some cities require 5 feet. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-R17 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A05
You may pass a bicyclist in a no-passing zone if it is safe, and after passing stay out of the lane until well clear; large vehicles and oversized loads need even more room. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-R16 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A05
Bicyclists are not required to ride in a bike lane and may leave it to turn left or avoid hazards. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables none [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A05
Low three-wheeled recumbent bikes and handcycles are hard to see despite mirrors and tall orange flags. [A05]
Why it matters: group bicycles; difficulty low; prereq none; confusables none [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A05
An autocycle is a three-wheeled motorcycle with safety belts, a roll bar or hoops and a steering wheel but no straddle seat, and it deserves the same watchfulness as a motorcycle. [A05]
Why it matters: group autocycles; difficulty medium; prereq none; confusables sec12-R11 [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A02
Slow-moving vehicles top out at 25 mph, but when following a horse you slow further, to 15 to 20 mph, and stay 20 feet back. [A02]
Why it matters: group slow vehicles; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-F15, sec12-F17 [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A01
A car needs about 130 feet to stop from 55 mph, but a commercial vehicle at that speed needs about 400 feet. [A01]
Why it matters: group trucks; difficulty high; prereq none; confusables sec12-F02 [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-mi-s:michigan-department-of-state-secretary-o:handbook:pdf-0067]

ranked.label: Never share a lane with a motorcycle
Bike lanes are optional for riders
